title: SV-DCD: Recovering Nonlinear Lagged Relations Across Recurrent Regimes with Partial Parameter Sharing
content: A past measurement can help predict another variable under some operating conditions and contribute little under others. With few observations per regime, it is difficult to determine which nonlinear lagged relations are shared across regimes. We propose SV-DCD for recurrent regimes with known labels. The method groups the basis coefficients for each candidate lagged relation and jointly estimates a shared reference and regime-specific deviations. The fitted coefficients identify the relations present in each regime and those shared by all regimes. We express the induced group penalty through a weighted geometric median, identify when the estimator reduces to independent fits, and derive conditional bounds for estimation error and graph recovery. Across 80 simulated cases, SV-DCD improved the mean of worst-regime and varying-edge F1 by 0.5009 over common-support regularization. The largest gain was in varying-edge F1. The ranking score changed less under rotation for SV-DCD than for the coordinate-wise estimator. Under high sharing and short sequences, SV-DCD improved shared-edge average precision by 0.1761 over independent group estimation.
